passage: In the changing room, some boys joked about Rafiq's height, and one called him "pocket size". Rafiq's ears went hot. He gave them no reaction, and when it happened again the next day he told his class teacher, who spoke to the boys. He kept comparing himself with both the tall boys and the late bloomers, until his older cousin told him, "Bodies grow at different speeds. Mine didn't move until much later." Rafiq shrugged, unsure, but began sleeping better. Across the corridor, Leela scrolled through fitness and beauty accounts every night and felt she had to change. One evening she noticed that most of them were selling something. "They want me to feel small so I will buy," she realised, and she unfollowed most of them. But the mirror still pulled at her; she checked it all day and thought about food constantly, feeling out of control. She told Pema, the school counsellor, who listened, said that asking for help is brave, and phoned Leela's parents that afternoon so they could see a doctor together.

qa.q: What did one boy call Rafiq in the changing room?
How did Rafiq's handling of the mockery differ from Leela's handling of the influencer accounts?
qa.a: Rafiq gave no reaction and told his class teacher when the jokes were repeated, while Leela noticed that most of the accounts were selling something and unfollowed most of them.

qa.q: What was Leela feeling about her body and food when she went to Pema?
qa.a: She felt inadequate and out of control, since she checked the mirror all day and thought about food constantly.

qa.q: What could Leela do next after Pema phoned her parents?
qa.a: She could see a doctor together with her parents and keep talking with Pema, since asking for help early is a strength.

grounding: Four teens meet body worries: mockery about height, comparing puberty, influencers that sell inadequacy, and an obsession with mirrors and food.
